## 1. Slow checkout: `PaymentClient.refreshSession` stalls every worker

`PaymentClient.authorize` calls `currentSession`. About once a second, `currentSession` calls `refreshSession`, and that call takes 311–453 ms. The refresh runs synchronously inside `authorize` on whichever thread hits it first. The other three workers stall for the same stretch.

- **Refresh cost:** across about 15 refreshes the durations were 311, 314, 324, 328, 342, 353, 361, 367, 371, 388, 404, 414, 425, 430, 433 and 453 ms. `currentSession` normally takes 0 ms.
- **Normal vs. slow:** normal `authorize` calls take about 18–46 ms. During a refresh they take 186–458 ms.
- **All four workers at once:** the slow `authorize` calls come in groups of four, one per `checkout-0` to `checkout-3`, finishing within about 10–15 ms of each other. One example is 268, 302, 303 and 392 ms at t=…348584–348593.
- **Timing:** the log shows a refresh starting every 0.3–1.1 s, each followed within about 400 ms by a group of four slow `authorize` calls.
- **Why it isn't an error:** the refresh succeeds. It is only slow, so nothing is logged.

The refresh looks like a single shared lock held while the refresh does remote work. I did not read the SDK bytecode, so the lock itself is inferred from the pattern above. The pattern is: one thread refreshes, and all four stall for the same duration.

## 2. Manual review: `FraudScreen.deepScore` times out and `screen` returns HOLD

`FraudScreen.screen` calls `deepScore`. When `deepScore` throws `RiskServiceException("deep scoring timed out for order …")`, `screen` catches it and returns `Verdict.HOLD`. `CheckoutServiceApp` then adds the order to `ReviewQueue`. The exception never reaches the service, so it doesn't appear in the error logs. The SDK is failing closed on its own timeouts, and those timeouts say nothing about the order's fraud risk.

- **One-to-one match:** in one full sampled window, 14 `deepScore` throws produced exactly 14 HOLD verdicts (identity `778d07d8`).
- **No other cause:** every `deepScore` call that returned normally produced PASS (identity `36b3e9e3`). I saw no HOLD without a preceding throw.
- **Rate:** roughly 1 in 3 to 1 in 4 of the `deepScore` calls I sampled threw. In the last window, `screen` calls that reached `deepScore` took 10–42 ms.
- **Timeout vs. normal duration:** throws take 10–32 ms and successful calls take 10–33 ms. The timeout is therefore not triggered by a long call. It looks like a very short timeout on the vendor side, or a failure inside `deepScore`.

## What I couldn't determine

- **Cause of the timeouts:** I don't know why `deepScore` times out. That could be the vendor's risk backend or an SDK-internal limit. I didn't trace into its inner calls.
- **Refresh and session lifetime:** I don't know whether the session expires that quickly by design or whether the SDK is refreshing needlessly. A refresh roughly every second suggests the session is being invalidated or the TTL is misconfigured.
- **Direct blocking evidence:** I didn't capture lock-wait stacks, so the shared lock is inferred.

## Suggested next steps

- Ask the vendor why `refreshSession` runs about every second and does remote work while holding up every caller. Also ask for a way to refresh in the background.
- Ask the vendor for a configurable `deepScore` timeout and an option to fail open, or to return a distinct "UNKNOWN" verdict.
- In this service, `CheckoutServiceApp.checkout` can't tell a real HOLD from a timeout-induced one. Until the SDK exposes that, track the review-queue rate against a baseline.
